Messages.Author: widmer christian
Messages.Body:
Robert J. Shmit (cully@ritz.mordor.com) wrote:
: How do you vote? Lets take the example of Ancient Influence:

: Ancient Influence, Action, Political Action
: +1 Stealth 	All Kindred
: POLITICAL CARD
: WORTH 1 VOTE
: [card text]

Ancient Influence: Name of the Vote (must be given when you call for a vote
so the others know what will hit them if they don't intercept)

Action, Political Action: Why 2x Action? I don't know, but it means that
this card is an action card for a political action (you can't get more
obvious, can you?)

+1 Stealth: The Vampire playing this vote does so at +1 Stealth,
 so: You announce you gonna make a political Action with Vampire X.
     The Action is bringing up the Vote "Ancient Influence"
     The Action is at +1 Stealth.
     If anyone wants to stop your Vampire from bringing up this vote he needs
     Intercept +1 or more.
     If not interceptet, the vote takes place.

All Kindred: Any Vampire can be used to bring up the vote. There are some
cards restricted e.g. to Prince or Justicar - these can obviously only be
brought up by a prince or a justicar.

Political Card worth one Vote: When the vote is not intercepted any
Prince/Primogen/Justicar can Vote (see rules: Prim: 1 Vote, Prince: 2
Votes, Justicar: 3 Votes). You can also use the edge for one vote (give it
back) plus any action modifiers/reaction cards (depending on who played the
vote only action modifiers (if you played it) or reactions (if another one
played it). OR you can throw in any POLITICAL CARDS (like this one) for the
value in votes (here: 1 vote - has anybody seen one with more votes?),
ignoring what kind of vote it is.
Then the votes are counted and the effect takes place (in case the vote was
accepted) or the vote failed and the card is discarded.

Christian

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
Robert J. Shmit <cully@ritz.mordor.com> wrote:
>Ancient Influence, Action, Political Action
>+1 Stealth 	All Kindred
>POLITICAL CARD
>WORTH 1 VOTE
>[card text]
>
>Lets disect this
>
>The +1 stealth I understand, but what does that All Kindred thing mean? Why
>does it have to say political card? Worth 1 Vote? HELP!

The "All Kindred" means the vote can only be called by a vampire, i.e.,
you can't tap an ally to call a vote.  Some political cards say "Prince or
Justicar", so can only be called by an appropriately titled vampire.  A few
of them even have clan symbols (mostly the <clan> Justicar votes), and can
only be called by vampires of that clan.

It says "Political Card, worth 1 vote" because during any vote, players
can burn political cards in their hand for 1 vote.  For example, if a vote
you called is deadlocked in a tie, you could burn a policard for a vote
in your favor.  Another player could then burn a policard for a vote against
you, and so on.

>Please, someone explain the voting process step by step.

1.  An appropriate vampire taps to call for the vote.  All people know at
	this point is which card is being played, not the terms of the vote,
	i.e. they won't know which clan will be tapped by Consanguineous
	Condemnation.  Note that you do replace the card used to call the
	vote in the first place, since it's being used as an action card.
2.  If the action is intercepted, then the action ends and combat ensues.
3.  Otherwise, the terms of the vote are set (e.g., the clan for CC
	is selected) and the vote beings.
4.  People cast votes (or abstain) until everyone is done.  Assume that if
	15 seconds pass without no one doing anything (casting a vote, or
	trying to convince someone to vote in their favor), then no more
	votes will be contributed.  A verbal countdown helps here.  Players
	get votes as per section 17.1; note that people don't get a "free"
	vote, except for the person calling the vote, who gets 1 vote by
	virtue of playing a political action card.
5.  If the vote passes, deal with its effects.


Tom Wylie		rec.games.deckmaster Network Representative for
aahz@hal.com			Wizards of the Coast, Inc.

Messages.Author: Campbell March
Messages.Body:
In article <CvsIII.Bp4@ritz.mordor.com> cully@ritz.mordor.com (Robert J. Shmit) writes:

> Ancient Influence
>   +1 Stealth 	All Kindred
>   POLITICAL CARD
>   WORTH 1 VOTE
>   The +1 stealth I understand, but what does that All Kindred thing mean? Why
>   does it have to say political card? Worth 1 Vote? HELP!
>
>   Please, someone explain the voting process step by step.

Gladly.   I have a fictional vampire, "Omar".   He has no stealth mods.

I decide to declare the Vote you outlined above.

(1) I Tap Omar, playing the Political Action card.   As stated, this
    action is now at +1 stealth.   The "All Kindred" qualifier means
    that only Vampires can call this vote; a non-vampire ally can't.
    If it said "Prince or Justicar only" only a Prince or Justicar could call
    it.
(2) The minions of my Prey or Predator may attempt to block this, as per
    any other action.   They'll need at least +1 intercept, of course.
    If intercept occurs, the card is discarded and combat occurs, as normal.
(3) No-one manages to block Omar, so the vote is now voted upon.
(4) Omar gets one vote for the card.   Any Primogen not in torpor or
    contested get 1 vote.   Any Princes get 2, Justicars 3.   Any Methuselah
    may play a card with the text "Political Card: Worth 1 vote" to gain 1
    vote.   The cards played thisd way have no other effect than votes.
(5) Once everyone has voted, if there's more votes for than against, the vote
    passes and the card's effect occurs.   If there's more against, or the
    vote is tied, the vote fails and the effect does not occur.
(6) Omar's action is finished.

Any more problems?

Sasquatch

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
Cerebus The Aardvark <kreme@netcom.com> wrote:
>>Ancient Influence: Name of the Vote (must be given when you call for a vote
>>so the others know what will hit them if they don't intercept)
>EXCUSE ME?  Where is THIS in the rules?

You always have to let people know what action you are taking before
they decide whether or not to block it.  Simply saying "I'm taking a
political action" doesn't cut it; you have to let people know which
political action you are taking, namely, Ancient Influence.  The rules
just say that if the vote has any terms, then those aren't revealed
unless the action is unblocked...  Not that you don't have to let
them see which action card is being used.

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
J Corley <jcorley@netcom.com> wrote:
>	When a political card says "worth one vote" does that include the 
>when it is the card you are voting on?  That is, does the person calling 
>the vote automatically get one vote from the card?

Yes, if you call a vote by virtue of a political action card (as opposed
to, say, a bloodhunt vote or a vote to burn Anarch Revolt), then the
action card you used gives you one vote.

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
Brian Scearce <bls@Eng.Sun.COM> wrote:
>> For example, if a vote you called is deadlocked in a tie,
>Isn't a tied vote just a failed vote?  I don't think "deadlock" is the
>right term for this.

When I was talking about a vote being deadlocked in a tie, I was talking
about an ongoing vote which people could still add votes to, where the
"yes" votes equalled the "no" votes, and everyone was debating whether
they really wanted to throw in another vote to break the tie.  If the voting
period ends, and the "yes" votes tie the "no" votes, then the vote
fails, yes.

>Isn't a tied vote just a failed vote?  I don't think "deadlock" is the
>right term for this.

When I was talking about a vote being deadlocked in a tie, I was talking
about an ongoing vote which people could still add votes to, where the
"yes" votes equalled the "no" votes, and everyone was debating whether
they really wanted to throw in another vote to break the tie.  If the voting
period ends, and the "yes" votes tie the "no" votes, then the vote
fails, yes.

In article <1994Sep12.005832.185@cam.compserv.utas.edu.au> cjudd@lawson.its.utas.edu.au (Craig Thomas Judd) writes:

> Do Primogens, Princes or Justicars tap to vote?  It seems from the discussion
> that they wouldn't, but I've seen a card (can't recall the name) which is
> played on a political action, which taps all of the abovementioned
> votegetters.  Now, there doesn't seem to be much point in this as
> they could still vote, unless they have to tap to do so.  Is it just
> meant to be an annoyance to  political players, or is it supposed to
> actually reduce their voting capability?

Correct; Primogen/Princes/Justicars do not tap to vote, and indeed can
vote while tapped.   My guess is that the card you're talking about is
designed to reduce someone's defences; ie "I call this vote" "I vote
with my 3 Primogen and 1 prince" "All vampires that participated in
this vote are tapped" "uh oh...I have no defence against your bleed"
